# irender-chart-kit

Charts for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents, drawn by [Apache ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org/) 6. Charts are fully reactive: they filter, group and drill through rows in the browser, write clicks, zooms, legends and brushes to state, and can take live data. Give `ui-chart` rows and a `type` for the common charts. For anything else ECharts can draw, give it a full ECharts `option`, or use both: the option is merged over what the shorthand builds. Charts follow the document's theme, including dark mode, and they work with [irender-ui-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md): put them in cards, drive them from its controls, and write clicks back to state.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_ui_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);      // optional
irender_chart_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);

let mut doc = irender_core::parse(src, irender_core::Format::Yaml)?;
irender_ui_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);               // optional
irender_chart_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);            // optional: the series colours, light and dark
let ir = engine.resolve(&doc)?;
```

From the CLI, add `--chart-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/charts/gallery.yaml --data examples/charts/gallery.data.json \
  --ui-kit --chart-kit -o charts.html
```

[`examples/charts/gallery.yaml`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/charts/gallery.yaml) has a chart for every ECharts example category.

```yaml
- type: ui-card
  props: { title: Orders, description: This week }
  children:
    - type: ui-chart
      props: { type: bar, data: "{{ week }}", x: day, y: [orders, returns], stack: true }
```

## Loading ECharts

ECharts is 1.1 MB (about 360 KB gzipped), so it isn't inlined. Pages with a chart load it once from [`ChartKit::src`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/src/lib.rs), and pages without one don't load it at all. The default is jsDelivr, pinned to `echarts@6.1.0`. To serve your own copy, or to use the SVG renderer:

```rust
irender_chart_kit::register_with(&mut engine.registry, irender_chart_kit::ChartKit {
    src: "/static/echarts.min.js".into(),
    renderer: irender_chart_kit::Renderer::Svg,
});
```

The kit's own script is about 10 KB gzipped and is added once per page. If the host page loads ECharts itself (`window.echarts`), the kit uses that copy. Extensions such as echarts-gl or custom series registered on it work too.

## `ui-chart`

| prop | |
|---|---|
| `type` | The series the shorthand builds (see below). Leave it out to use `option` alone. |
| `data` | Rows: objects (`{ day: Mon, orders: 120 }`) or arrays (`[Mon, 120]`, with `x`/`y` as column numbers). Plain numbers are fine too; their position is the category. |
| `x` | The category or name field. Default: the first field. |
| `y` | Value field(s): `orders`, `[orders, returns]`, or `{ field, name, …series options }` per series. Default: every other numeric field. |
| `value` | A third field: the heatmap's cell value or a scatter point's size. |
| `links` | `{ source, target, value }` for `sankey`, `graph` and `chord`. Nodes are taken from `data`, or from the links. |
| `filter`, `aggregate`, `series`, `sort`, `limit` | Shape the rows before drawing; see [Filters and grouping](#filters-and-grouping). |
| `drill` | Fields to click down through, e.g. `[region, country, city]`; see [Drill-downs](#drill-downs). |
| `xType` | `category`, `time`, `value` or `log`. Default: `time` when every x is a date or epoch milliseconds, on lines and points. |
| `zoom` | Zoom along the category or time axis: `inside` (wheel and drag), `slider`, or `both` (`true`). |
| `brush` | Drag to select points: `rect` (`true`), `polygon`, `lineX` or `lineY`. |
| `live` | Live data for this chart; see [Live data](#live-data). |
| `option` | An [ECharts option](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html), merged over the shorthand's. Arrays of objects (`series`, `xAxis`, …) merge by position, like ECharts' own merge. Data arrays are replaced. |
| `stack`, `smooth`, `horizontal`, `labels` | Shorthand switches. |
| `format`, `currency`, `decimals` | How values show in labels, tooltips and the value axis, in the document's `lang`: `number` (the default), `currency` (`currency`, default `USD`) or `percent` (of 1), with `decimals` digits after the point. Without them, labels and tooltips show at most two decimals; with a `format`, big axis values stay short (`$1.5M`). |
| `legend`, `tooltip` | On or off. Default: a legend with two or more series, and a tooltip always. |
| `height` | Number (px) or CSS length. Default 320; a gantt's default fits its rows (or `visibleRows` of them). The width is the container's. |
| `columns`, `markers`, `today`, `visibleRows`, `workdays`, `holidays`, `critical`, `baselines` | For a gantt; see [Gantt](#gantt). |
| `loading` | Shows the loading mask, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`. |
| `bind`, `bindRow`, `bindZoom`, `bindLegend`, `bindBrush`, `bindDrill` | State keys for what people do with the chart; see [Interactions as state](#interactions-as-state). |
| `maps` | GeoJSON maps to register before drawing: `{ world: /geo/world.json }`. The URLs are checked against the policy. |
| `group` | Charts in one group share tooltips and zoom (`echarts.connect`). |
| `renderer` | `canvas` or `svg`, for this chart. |
| `title` | Accessible name. ECharts' own description of the data follows it. |

`ui-sparkline` is a small chart with no axes, legend or padding, for stat cards and table cells. It takes `data` (numbers, or rows with `y`), `type` (`area`, `line` or `bar`), `width`, `height` (default 40), `tooltip`, `option` and `live`.

### Shorthand types

| `type` | `data` | `x` / `y` |
|---|---|---|
| `line`, `area`, `bar`, `pictorialBar` | rows | category / value field(s) |
| `scatter`, `effectScatter` | rows | x / y field(s); `value` sizes the points |
| `candlestick` | rows | date / `[open, close, low, high]`, found by name when the fields are called that |
| `boxplot` | rows | group / one field of raw samples (the quartiles are computed), or five fields: min, Q1, median, Q3, max |
| `pie`, `donut`, `funnel` | rows | name / value field |
| `radar` | rows: one polygon each | name / one field per axis |
| `heatmap` | rows | column / row field; `value` colours the cell |
| `gauge` | a number, `{ name, value }`, one object with the value in `y` (e.g. a live reading), or rows | name / value |
| `tree` | `{ name, children }` | |
| `treemap`, `sunburst` | `[{ name, value, children }]` | |
| `sankey`, `graph`, `chord` | nodes (optional; a `category` field colours graph nodes) plus `links` | |
| `themeRiver` | rows | date / one stream per field |
| `parallel` | rows: one line each | / one axis per field; text fields become category axes |
| `gantt` | rows: one task each | fixed fields; see [Gantt](#gantt) |

Everything else goes in `option`: maps and `lines`, `custom` series, calendars, the `matrix` coordinate system, polar charts, `dataset` with transforms, `dataZoom`, `visualMap`, `markLine`, `graphic`, and 3D with echarts-gl. The gallery shows a calendar, polar bars and a sorted dataset written that way.

## State

Every prop can use state, so a chart redraws when the state it reads changes. That includes `{{ }}` anywhere inside `option`:

```yaml
- { type: ui-toggle-group, props: { bind: kind, options: [bar, line, area] } }
- type: ui-chart
  props:
    type: "{{ kind }}"
    data: "{{ results }}"            # e.g. filled by a `submit` with `into: results`
    loading: "{{ fetching }}"
    option: { title: { text: "{{ heading }}" } }
```

Server data is filled in at render time, and only the parts that read state are evaluated in the browser. A redraw that keeps the type and the components merges into the chart on screen, so values animate. A redraw that changes them starts over.

Clicks go the other way. Bind the chart, then load details for what was clicked:

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: bar, data: "{{ regions }}", bind: region }
  on:
    change: { action: submit, method: GET, endpoint: "/api/regions/{{ region }}", into: regionSales }
- { type: ui-chart, props: { type: donut, data: "{{ regionSales }}" } }
```

## Filters and grouping

Rows go through these steps, in order, before they are drawn. Each prop can read state, so a control bound to a state key filters every chart that uses it.

1. **`drill`**: the current level's rows (see below).
2. **`filter`**: an object of field → condition. A row is kept when every condition holds:

   | condition | keeps rows whose field… |
   |---|---|
   | `Europe`, `3` | equals it. Text and numbers compare loosely, so `"3"` from a form control matches `3`. |
   | `[Laptops, Phones]` | is one of them. A list of rows compares the same field of each, so `"{{ picked }}"` from `bindBrush` works. |
   | `{ from, to }` | is in the range, ends included. Dates compare as dates, numbers as numbers. This is the shape `bindZoom` writes. |
   | `{ gt, gte, lt, lte }` | compares that way. |
   | `{ contains: text }` | contains the text, ignoring case and accents. |
   | `{ empty: true }`, `{ empty: false }` | has no value (null, missing or `""`), or has one. |
   | `{ not: … }` | fails the inner condition. |
   | a row, e.g. from `bindRow` | equals that row's same field. |

   Blank conditions (null, `""`, `[]`, or `{ from: null }`) keep every row. A filter bound to an empty control shows everything rather than nothing. irender-ui-kit's `ui-filters` writes this format, so its panel can filter charts directly.
3. **`aggregate`**: `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max` or `count`. Groups rows by `x`, and by `series` if set, and aggregates the `y` fields. Each group also gets a `count`. With `count`, `y` defaults to it.
4. **`sort`**: a field, `-field` for descending, `{ field, order }`, or a list of these. With `series`, it orders the categories, each by its total over the series (`-amount`: the biggest totals first), and `limit` keeps the first N categories with all their series.
5. **`limit`**: the first N rows (with `series`, the first N categories).

`series: product` turns long-format rows (`{ month, product, amount }`) into one series per product, aligned on the categories.

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props:
    type: bar
    data: "{{ orders }}"          # every order, once, in state
    x: city
    y: amount
    aggregate: sum
    sort: -amount
    limit: 5
    filter: { product: "{{ products }}", date: "{{ range }}", region: "{{ region }}", channel: { not: Store } }
```

## Drill-downs

`drill` lists the fields to click down through. The chart starts grouped by the first field (summed unless `aggregate` says otherwise). Clicking a bar or slice filters to it and groups by the next field. A trail at the top left (`‹ All › Europe`) goes back up a level. The marks morph between levels.

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: bar, data: "{{ orders }}", drill: [region, country, city], y: amount, sort: -amount, bindDrill: geoPath }
- { type: ui-button, props: { label: Top }, on: { click: { action: set_state, key: geoPath, value: [] } } }
```

`bindDrill` keeps the path (`[Europe, Germany]`) in state, both ways. Other kinds of drill-down need no special support:
- **Into another chart:** `bind` the clicked item, and `filter` the other chart by it.
- **Into the server:** react to `on: { change: … }` with a `submit` that fetches details `into` state.
- **To another page:** `navigate` from `on.change`.
- **Within a hierarchy:** `treemap` and `sunburst` zoom into a node when it's clicked.

## Gantt

`type: gantt` draws a plan: a table of tasks on the left and their bars on a timeline, dates along the top.

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props:
    type: gantt
    data: "{{ tasks }}"
    series: team                                   # colours, with a legend
    columns: [name, { field: owner, name: Owner, width: 120 }]
    markers: [{ at: "2026-12-21", name: Beta freeze }]
    zoom: true
    bindRow: task
```

Each row is a task with these fields. Any other field can be a column.

| field | |
|---|---|
| `id` | What `group` and `after` refer to. Default: `name`. |
| `name` | The task's name, in the first column. |
| `start`, `end` | Dates (`2026-11-02`), timestamps or epoch milliseconds. A plain date as the `end` means the whole of that day. |
| `group` | The `id` of the row this one sits under. A row with rows under it is a group: its bar spans them, its progress is theirs weighted by length, and clicking its name (or its bar) closes and opens it. `collapsed: true` on a group starts it closed. |
| `progress` | 0 to 100. The part done is drawn solid, the rest faded. |
| `after` | The `id` (or a list) of the tasks this one waits for. Each gets an arrow from its end to this task's start; an arrow to a hidden task goes to its closed group. |
| `milestone` | `true`, or a `start` with no `end`: a diamond. |
| `color` | This bar's colour, over the series colour. |
| `baselineStart`, `baselineEnd` | The planned dates, read as `start` and `end` are; see `baselines`. |

- **`columns`**: the table's columns, each a field or `{ field, name, width, align }`. The first holds the names, indented under their groups. Default `[name]`. On a narrow chart the table takes at most half the width: the last columns go first, then the names get narrower.
- **`series`**: a field to colour the bars by, with a legend that hides a series' bars.
- **`markers`**: dated lines down the timeline, `[{ at, name, color }]`, named under it.
- **`today`**: a line at today's date when it falls on the timeline. Default true.
- **`workdays`**: tasks dated in whole days count and move on working days. `true` is Monday to Friday; a list names the weekdays that work, `0` for Sunday (`[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` for Sunday to Thursday). `holidays` adds dates off. Days off are shaded on the timeline, lengths read "5 working days", a moved task (by a drag or Alt and the arrows) lands on a working day and keeps its working days, its start or end steps over days off, and with `cascade` a task that waits starts on the first working day after what it waits for. Tasks with times of day keep to calendar days.
- **`critical`**: marks the critical path: the tasks with no slack, whose delay would move the plan's end. A task's slack is the least, over the tasks waiting on it (its `after`s, the other way), of the gap to that task plus that task's own slack; with nothing waiting, the gap to the last end. With `workdays` the gaps count working days, so a weekend or holiday before the next task isn't slack. Critical bars and milestones are ringed in red, the links between them drawn solid red, their rows and tooltips say "On the critical path", and a late link (one that starts before what it waits for ends) is dashed red. Groups aren't marked themselves, and a task that waits on a group waits on the group's span.
- **`baselines`**: a task with a `baselineStart` and `baselineEnd` (the dates first planned) gets a thin grey bar under its bar from them, and a milestone with a `baselineStart` a hollow diamond behind it, so a slip shows at a glance. A group's baseline spans its tasks' unless it has its own. Tooltips and rows say "Planned 2 Mar – 6 Mar" and how many days (working days with `workdays`) the end is late or early. Moving a bar leaves its baseline where it was. Default true; `false` hides them, e.g. from a switch in state.
- **`visibleRows`**: the chart is at most that many rows tall, and the rest scroll inside it: with the wheel, a thin bar on the right, dragging (when the bars don't move), or the keys on the table, which scroll to the row they go to. The dates and the table's header stay put, and zooming the timeline leaves the rows where they are.
- **`zoom`**: `true` adds −, + and "show all" buttons. ⌘/Ctrl with the wheel zooms, dragging pans, and Shift with the wheel pans. `slider` or `both` adds a slider. `bindZoom` works as for other charts.
- **Clicks:** `bind` and `bindRow` get the clicked task, and a group opening or closing fires `toggle` with `{ id, open, row }`.
- **Editing:** with `bindData` (the state key `data` reads), drag a bar to move its task, or either end to change its start or end, a day at a time; the bar shows where it's going and the tasks change when it's let go. On a touch screen, hold the bar for a moment first, so a quick swipe still scrolls; Escape puts a drag back. On a focused row, Alt with Left or Right moves the task a day, and with Shift too moves its end. Groups follow their tasks, and a milestone moves its date. New dates are written as the old ones were: a day stays a day, a timestamp a timestamp. Each edit fires `edit` with `{ id, start, end, row }`, and is announced. `editable: false` turns it off; while editable, dragging the background doesn't pan (Shift with the wheel, or the slider, does).
- **Conflicts:** a task that starts before one in its `after` ends gets a dashed red arrow, and its tooltip and row say `Starts before Orders API ends`.
- **Links:** while editable, a dot shows after a bar on hover. Drag from it onto another task to make that task wait on this one (added to its `after`); a link that would go round in a circle is refused, and said so. Click an arrow to remove its link. From the keyboard, press L on a task's row in the table, move to the task that waits for it and press Enter (Enter on a task that already waits for it removes the link; Escape stops). Each fires `link` with `{ from, to, added }` and is announced.
- **Cascade:** with `cascade: true`, moving or stretching a task (or adding a link) moves on the tasks that wait on it, and those that wait on them, as far as they must to start when what they wait for ends, keeping their length. The drag shows them moving, and `edit` lists them in `pushed`.
- **Height:** without `height`, the chart is as tall as its rows, and it grows and shrinks as groups open and close.

**Keyboard and screen readers.** The table is HTML laid over the chart: a `treegrid` named by `title`, with a row per task that a screen reader reads as its name, dates, length, progress and series. Tab reaches it; Up and Down move between rows (Home and End to the ends), Right opens a group or steps into it, Left closes it or goes to the group above, and Enter or Space opens a group or picks a task as a click on its bar does (`bind`, `bindRow`). The focused task shows its tooltip, and the picked one is marked, following `bindRow`.

## Interactions as state

| prop | state holds | from state |
|---|---|---|
| `bind` | the clicked item's name (its x, or value). Clicking it again clears it, so a click works as a toggled filter. | selects (highlights) that item |
| `bindRow` | the clicked item's row (after grouping) | |
| `bindZoom` | the zoom window as `{ from, to }` in axis values (categories, dates in the data's own format, or numbers), or null when it shows everything | zooms there; null zooms out |
| `bindLegend` | the names of the visible series (or slices) | shows only those; null shows all |
| `bindBrush` | the rows inside the brushed area | `[]` clears the brush |
| `bindDrill` | the drill path | goes to that level |

Each interaction also fires a bubbling DOM event for `on:` actions: `change` (a click), `drill`, `zoom`, `legend` and `brush`. `bindZoom` works without `zoom` too: the window then moves only from state. Writing the zoom state on one chart and a `filter: { date: "{{ range }}" }` on others gives the classic overview-and-detail dashboard. The gallery's "Drill-downs, filters and live data" section wires all of these together.

## Live data

A chart's `live` prop, or the `ui-live-data` component, keeps data coming in:

```yaml
# One source in state, for any number of components:
- type: ui-live-data
  props: { url: /api/metrics, every: 1000, mode: append, window: 300, key: time,
           into: metrics, status: feedStatus, paused: "{{ !liveOn }}", params: { host: "{{ host }}" } }
- { type: ui-chart, props: { type: line, data: "{{ metrics }}", x: time, y: [cpu, memory], zoom: inside } }
- { type: ui-badge, props: { text: "{{ feedStatus }}" } }

# Or straight into one chart:
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: scatter, x: time, y: amount, xType: time,
           live: { url: /api/orders/stream, stream: true, mode: append, window: 100, key: id } }
```

| setting | |
|---|---|
| `url` | Polled with GET. With `stream: true` it is read as server-sent events, and `ws://` / `wss://` URLs are WebSockets. It may use state. Script URLs are refused, and a URL known on the server must pass the policy. |
| `every` | Milliseconds between polls (default 5000, at least 250). The next poll waits for the previous response, and polling waits while the tab is hidden. |
| `mode` | `replace` (default): each message is the data. `append`: messages (a row or a list of rows) are added. |
| `window` | With `append`, keep the last N rows (default 500). |
| `key` | With `append`, a row with the same value in this field replaces the old one. Use it for upserts, or to make a re-sent row harmless. |
| `pick` | A path to the data inside each message, e.g. `data.items`. |
| `params` | Query parameters. Blank ones are left out, so filters can go to the server: `{ from: "{{ range.from }}" }`. A change reconnects at once. |
| `paused` | Disconnects while true. |
| `into` | A state key that gets the data (required on `ui-live-data`). On a chart it's optional, and shares the chart's data. |
| `status` | A state key set to `connecting`, `live`, `paused` or `error`. The element also carries `data-live` (chart) or `data-status`. |

WebSockets reconnect with backoff up to 30 s, and EventSource reconnects by itself. Live data goes through the same filters, grouping and drill as any other data, and when the type and components stay the same the chart animates new points in. For the gallery's live charts, serve the examples with `python3 examples/serve.py`, which adds a polled metrics endpoint and an order stream.

## Functions

ECharts takes functions in some places: formatters, `renderItem` for custom series, symbol sizes. A document is JSON, so it names a function, and the host page provides it:

```yaml
option: { yAxis: { axisLabel: { formatter: { $fn: money } } } }
```

```html
<script>window.irenderChartFunctions = { money: (v) => "$" + v.toLocaleString() };</script>
```

Functions are looked up whenever the chart draws, so define them in an ordinary script on the page. A document can only use the functions the host defines. Many formatters don't need a function at all: ECharts' string templates such as `"{b}: {c}"` work as they are.

## Theme

The kit reads the page's CSS tokens and turns them into an ECharts theme:
- Text uses `color.text` and `color.muted`.
- Axis and grid lines use `color.border`.
- Tooltips, and the gaps between slices and cells, use `color.surface`.
- Series colours come from `color.chart-1` … `color.chart-8`.

Values such as `color-mix()` are resolved by the browser first. A missing token falls back to the element's own colours, so charts look right without any theme.

`apply_theme` adds eight series colours. Each has its own step for dark mode, and they're in an order where neighbouring colours stay distinct for colour-blind readers. The heatmap's sequential scale runs from `chart-1` down into the surface colour. When the colour scheme changes, or a theme attribute (`class`, `style`, `data-theme`) changes on `<html>` or `<body>`, every chart restyles itself, as it does when a theme option is picked.

`apply_theme` also adds a `chart` theme option, the colour scheme:
- **Default** follows irender-ui-kit's palette: with a coloured one (Rose, Blue, Green, Orange, Violet) charts take its shades, with custom colours they take a scheme built from them, and with a neutral one (Zinc, Slate, Stone) they take the eight hues above. A palette names its series colours `color.palette-chart-1` … `8`; a theme of your own can set them too.
- **Hues**: the eight hues above, whatever the palette.
- **Blue, Rose, Green, Orange and Violet**: shades of one colour, as the UI kit's palettes of those names.
- **Mono**: greys.
- **Custom**: eight colours built from the custom primary and second brand colour picked with irender-ui-kit's `ui-theme-colors`.

A scheme picked here wins over the palette's. Pick it with irender-ui-kit's `{ type: ui-theme-option, props: { option: chart, swatch: color.chart-1 } }`, or add schemes of your own under `theme.options.chart.choices`.

Defaults follow common charting practice:
- 2 px lines.
- Bars rounded at the data end.
- Value axes without an axis line, and faint grid lines.
- Category labels shown wherever they fit.
- A tooltip on every chart.
- No animation for people who ask their system for reduced motion.

ECharts' `aria` description is on, so screen readers get a summary of the data.

## Lifecycle

- A chart starts once it has a size, so charts in closed tabs, dialogs and `if`s start when they're shown.
- It follows its container's size.
- It is disposed of when it leaves the page (an `if` that hides it, a list rebuilt from state), and drawn again if it comes back.

## Untrusted documents

ECharts tooltips are HTML. With [`Engine::untrusted`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-html/src/lib.rs) (any policy that blocks event attributes or unsafe URLs):
- Tooltip `formatter` strings are escaped. Line breaks (`<br>`) still work.
- `extraCssText` is dropped.
- `title.link` must not be a `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:` URL.
- Map URLs are checked against the policy.

Data values in tooltips are escaped by ECharts itself. Functions can only be ones the host defines.

## Tests

```sh
cargo test -p irender-chart-kit                                   # rendering and config
cargo test -p irender-chart-kit --test browser -- --ignored       # in Chrome: every type, drill, filters, zoom, legend, brush, live data, theme, lifecycle, gantt
ECHARTS=path/to/echarts.min.js cargo test -p irender-chart-kit --test browser -- --ignored   # offline
```
